hook_text: Charge it for three seconds, touch it to an LED, and watch the LED flare and die. That is a capacitor.
clip_script: Two plates, an insulator between. Connect a battery and charge piles up until the capacitor's volts match. Disconnect: it holds. Touch an LED: it empties into the LED, flare and fade. Size is capacitance, in microfarads. Charge it through a resistor and it fills fast, then slower. Ohms times farads is seconds: 10 kilohms and 100 microfarads is one second. That is how timers work. Small discs go either way. Big cans have a stripe on the minus leg; backwards or over-voltaged, they swell and pop. Check the stripe, check the volts, drain it through a resistor before you touch it.
visual_style: Whiteboard two plates filling with plus and minus; an LED flaring and fading; a charging curve flattening; R x C = 1 s; an electrolytic can with a stripe and a plus warning.
pacing: Charge, hold, flare, size, curve, timer, discs, cans, safety.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and time how long a 1000 microfarad capacitor keeps an LED visibly lit.
